results.content: # Trump approval rating falls to career low in new poll. President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to a new record low, with less than one-third of Americans approving of the president’s job performance, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll. results.content: # Trump approval ticks up as GOP trails before midterms: poll. After weeks of record lows stretching back to late September, President Donald Trump's approval rating ticked up slightly, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll. The poll, released on Oct. 26, found Trump’s approval at 32%, up one percentage point from last week's Reuters/Ipsos tracking, when his approval rating hit a record low across his White House terms. The latest Reuters/Ipsos poll gives Democrats an 11-point advantage, down 1 point from the previous week’s record high. results.content: With the midterm elections less than two weeks away, Trump has the lowest approval rating of any president since Harry Truman in 1946, a new New York Times/Siena poll released this week revealed. That year, Truman’s approval rating hit 33% — just 1 percentage point lower than Trump, the survey showed. A CNN/SSRS poll, released Wednesday, noted that Trump’s approval rating is 32%, which is a new low. A Reuters/Ipsos poll from Monday showed Trump with a record low approval rating of 31%. An NBC News survey, out the day before, found that the president’s approval rating slipped to 34% among U.S. adults, a second-term low.
